text:
A falsifiable design: before training, record each diagnostic’s predicted intervention, direction of HR@10 change, affected users/categories, minimum meaningful gain, and failure criterion. Compare three prespecified models: baseline, diagnostic-guided intervention, and matched control. Match perturbation count, history lengths, item popularity/recency, training updates, and compute; randomize which eligible interactions receive the control perturbation. Keep seeds and evaluation candidates identical. Improvement over baseline alone cannot establish diagnostic specificity; the guided intervention must also outperform its matched control. Three models provide one controlled case study, insufficient to establish general predictive validity across interventions.

Estimate uncertainty from paired per-user hit differences. Bootstrap users within each category, preserving all three models’ outcomes together, then average the four category differences equally. Report category effects, macro difference, 95% intervals, and discordant hit counts. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on trained models and fixed candidates; they exclude training-seed and negative-sampling variability. The pinned 99-negative HR@10 remains the required endpoint, but sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model rankings, limiting interpretation. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

Prespecify primary contrasts, multiplicity handling, checkpoint rules, and a GPU-budget stopping rule; log every attempted configuration. Repeatedly choosing models on the same validation users creates selection optimism: ordinary bootstrap intervals and adjustment for only the final three models do not account for the preceding adaptive search. Treat validation findings as exploratory, freeze the selected model, and leave confirmation to the host’s independent held-out evaluation. Under limited compute, prioritize the controlled comparison over additional adaptive variants. These recommendations follow the adaptive-holdout validity problem demonstrated by [Dwork et al.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26250683/).
